PASS on the fake backend only (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level); the package is model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null), no hardware was attached and no hardware or real-engine run is claimed. The card's entry symbol humanoid.scripts.sim2sim:run_mujoco exists at humanoid/scripts/sim2sim.py:87, but it takes a TorchScript policy and a Sim2simCfg defined only under __main__, exposes no reset, step or seed of its own, and its module imports humanoid.envs (Isaac Gym), so this package serves the card's models[1], resources/robots/XBot/mjcf/XBot-L.xml, through MujocoDriver instead of importing or running the upstream script. That model is the one Sim2simCfg selects when --terrain is absent (sim2sim.py:178-182); the card's models[0], XBot-L-terrain.xml, is not served. The decision family-config and helper MujocoDriver can express this interface, so there is no deviation from the card. The read-only clone was read in place at commit ae46e201c85a2b17e7f2cea59a441dae7ea88a8f; no file of it was written. The MJCF has three base slide joints plus one ball joint and twelve leg hinges (19 qpos, 18 qvel), and twelve motor actuators with ctrllimited true and ctrlrange -200 to 200 (XBot-L.xml:165-168, :394-481, :497-510). The bridge derives the cap.world.step.v1 ctrl envelope from that model range and refuses an out-of-range value before writing data.ctrl; ticks is bounded by the bridge (1 to 10000). The driver declares no Limit of its own, no operator-required bound and no site-limits.example.json is needed. cap.world.reset.v1 runs mj_resetData + mj_forward and restores the parsed model qpos0; the class seed is accepted but a MuJoCo reset does not use it. The served integration step is the MJCF's own 0.001 s (XBot-L.xml:3); the upstream loop overwrites it with its own 0.001 s dt and writes PD torques clipped to 200 (sim2sim.py:98-99, :155-160, :190), but this package does not run that loop and takes the caller's control vector directly. mujoco is not installed here (importing it raises ModuleNotFoundError), so backends['fake'] is the package's pure Python stand-in mujoco module in fake.py (class FakeMujoco). The stand-in parses the same MJCF for the three slides, the ball base, the twelve hinges, the twelve motors, their explicit ctrlranges and the 0.001 s step, but integrates a placeholder velocity proportional to each control value and holds the base fixed; it loads no STL mesh, resolves no contact, inertia, gravity, constraint, damping or actuator dynamics, and does not implement mj_getState/mj_setState. The fidelity gaps list every difference; no trajectory was compared with MuJoCo. The real mujoco path (a backend name that backends does not list) was not run. WARNINGS kept from the last gate run (all expected, none failed): G6.NOT_RECORDED and G7.UPSTREAM_BACKEND because backends['fake'] is the package's FakeMujoco class object, which the gate does not wrap in a Recorder, so native calls are not recorded and G7 has no fake surface to check; G8.NO_UNIT x3 for the bridge-derived inputs ticks, action.ctrl[*] and seed, which are expected for simulator families. No G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warning was raised. TESTS: test_driver.py keeps the required mhs.testing.check_driver(HERE, backend='fake') call and adds six cases (model shape from the card model, control-envelope refusal with zero effect, step advancing the integration state and keeping the control, reset to the model defaults, published fidelity contract, e-stop latch); they pass. No catalogue_requests: the package uses only cap.world.step.v1 and cap.world.reset.v1. No NOT COVERED array: the fake carries the full 19 qpos, 18 qvel and 12 ctrl arrays, not a smaller stand-in.
